title: Free quotient resolutions and complete free cells over completed coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and put $R_{n,T}=(R/\varpi^n)_T$ and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_{n,T}$, using constant sheaves and inverse limits [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A complex $M$ is quotient-tower complete if its canonical quotient maps exhibit it as $R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})$, with the quotient transitions and with the terms restricted to $B_T$-scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then for every $n\geq1$ the canonical augmented complex $[B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_T]\to R_{n,T}$, with its two free terms in degrees $-1,0$, is a quasi-isomorphism and is K-flat: its tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Every finite sum $B_T^{\oplus r}$ placed in any single degree is quotient-tower complete, through its actual quotient projections. For every $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$, without a boundedness assumption, the canonical reduction fits into a distinguished triangle
$$M\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}M\longrightarrow \operatorname{Res}(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})\longrightarrow M[1].$$
The middle arrow is induced by $B_T\to R_{n,T}$.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, completed coefficient modules in the opening and top-generator triangle; supporting Tag 099I, algebraization.tex, lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence. proof.text: Write $\underline R$ for the constant coefficient ring sheaf. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $R$ is a domain and a principal ideal ring, and $\varpi\ne0$. Thus every ideal is finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian, and multiplication by $\varpi^n$ is injective for every $n\ge1$. The module sequence $0\to R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R\to R/\varpi^n\to0$ is exact: its quotient has exactly the kernel $\varpi^nR$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties] on each site object. This gives $0\to\underline R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}\underline R\to R_{n,T}\to0$; the same clause applied to the surjections $R/\varpi^{n+1}\to R/\varpi^n$ shows that the constant-sheaf transition maps are surjective on sections, hence epimorphisms.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; regular-uniformizer specialization using the cited DVR statement

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] with $A=R$ and $I=(\varpi)$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1, and its $B$ is exactly $B_T$. Flatness makes tensoring the exact sequence of step 1 with $B_T$ exact. The tensor-unit identification sends its first map to multiplication by $\varpi^n$. The lemma's canonical reduction isomorphism identifies its last term $B_T\otimes_{\underline R}R_{n,T}$ with $R_{n,T}$: flatness identifies ordinary and derived tensor, and the reduction sends $b\otimes\bar r$ to $q_n(b)\bar r$, where $q_n:B_T\to R_{n,T}$ is the specified projection. We obtain $0\to B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_T\xrightarrow{q_n}R_{n,T}\to0$. Consequently $P_n=[B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_T]$, in degrees $-1,0$, has zero cohomology in degree $-1$ and $R_{n,T}$ in degree $0$; its actual augmentation $\epsilon_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat, applied to all powers of the principal ideal

proof.text: The sheaf $B_T$ is flat as a module over itself because tensoring with it is the identity functor. Thus $P_n$ is a bounded-above complex of flat $B_T$-modules, and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes it K-flat. The same argument applies to $B_T^{\oplus r}$ concentrated in any one degree: its tensor functor is a finite direct sum of copies of the identity, so its terms are flat.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (the cited node gives this statement although its source metadata says 06YS)

proof.text: First take $F=B_T^{\oplus r}$ in degree $0$. Its K-flat model from step 3 computes scalar extension by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], giving $F\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T}=R_{n,T}^{\oplus r}$ with the quotient projection on every coordinate. These identifications commute with the quotient transitions because they send $b e_j\otimes\bar a$ to $q_n(b)\bar a\,e_j$. Regard this tower as a tower of $B_T$-modules. Its transitions are epimorphisms by step 1, so [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] identifies its derived limit with its ordinary limit, with the actual projections. This ordinary limit is $B_T^{\oplus r}$: a compatible family of $r$-tuples is exactly $r$ compatible families, each in $\lim_n R_{n,T}=B_T$. This proves the required quotient-tower completeness. For a free cell in degree $d$, the identical calculation shifts the Roos triangle by $[-d]$; shifts preserve distinguished triangles and products, the latter because shifting is an equivalence. Hence its derived limit is $B_T^{\oplus r}[-d]$, with precisely the shifted quotient projections. The argument includes $r=0$.

source.place: Propositions 3.1.9-3.1.10, pp. 17-18, with 3.2.3(1) and 4.2.8; finite coordinates and shifts of the Roos triangle

proof.text: For arbitrary, possibly unbounded $M$, choose a representative and a K-flat resolution $Q\to M$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $Q\otimes_{B_T}R_{n,T}$ represents $M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T}$ in $D(R_{n,T})$. After restriction this is the same underlying complex of $B_T$-modules. Since $Q$ is K-flat, tensoring with $Q$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs]. In particular $\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_{B_T}P_n)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_n}Q\otimes_{B_T}R_{n,T}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This identifies the former complex with the scalar restriction of the derived reduction. The composite $Q\to\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes P_n)\to Q\otimes R_{n,T}$, using inclusion of the degree-zero term of $P_n$, sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$. It is exactly the canonical scalar-extension map, since $\epsilon_n$ in degree zero is $q_n$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism); derived change of rings via K-flat models

proof.text: With the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $P_n=\operatorname{Cone}(\varpi^n:B_T[0]\to B_T[0])$. Apply [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] to $Q$ and this map. Tensor-unit identifications give $\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes P_n)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(\varpi^n:Q\to Q)$, compatibly with inclusion of the second $Q$. Its cone triangle is distinguished by the definition of the derived triangulation. Substituting the quasi-isomorphism of step 5 into this triangle gives $M\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}M\to\operatorname{Res}(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})\to M[1]$. The inclusion compatibility and the formula $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ in step 5 identify the middle arrow with the map induced by $q_n$, not just an unspecified morphism with isomorphic target. No boundedness of $Q$ or $M$ was used.
